newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch flower auction proposes major restructure.
newsitem.headline: Dutch flower auction proposes major restructure.

text.p: Bloemenveiling Aalsmeer, the Dutch flower auction , has announced a restructuring plan designed to safeguard its position as the biggest market place of its kind in the world.
The auction's management said in a statement it will split itself into two independent units, one dealing with the international market and a second grouping together sales and marketing activities.

Aalsmeer's managers said they want to boost turnover of the auction to 3.7 billion guilders in the year 2000. Aalsmeer had a turnover of 2.4 billion guilders last year, and a net profit of 13.5 million guilders.
The restructuring plan calls for two completely separate organisations operating under one roof, the auction said, noting in its statement that it is still auctioning the way it did 80 years ago.
A new management team is also to be brought in, and existing managing director Andre Mulder has said he will step down.

The programme will take some four years to achieve management said. The new sales and marketing unit will be open to auction members to enable them to reinforce their competitive positions, while studies will be set in place to strengthen the market's international position.
The proposed changes have yet to be approved by the auction's members and regional boards, the statement added. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
